summary: If someone is taken out of his Shabbos area against his will, he may only walk four amos. The Rabbis argue about a person brought into a city or a pen, and the mishnah tells a story about Sages on a boat.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּהוּ גוֹיִם אוֹ רוּחַ רָעָה,
chunks.en: Someone who was taken out by non-Jews, or by a bad spirit,
chunks.explain: The bad spirit made him not in his right mind for a while.
chunks.st: With regard to one whom gentiles forcibly took him out beyond the Shabbat limit, or if an evil spirit took him out,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he was temporarily insane, and found himself outside the Shabbat limit,

chunks.en: has only four amos to walk.
chunks.st: he has only four cubits
chunks.stMore: that he may walk from where he is standing.

chunks.en: If they brought him back, it is as if he never left.
chunks.st: If the gentiles returned him, or if he came back while still under the influence of the evil spirit, it is as though he had never left
chunks.stMore: his Shabbat limit, and he may move about within his original limit as before.

chunks.en: If they brought him to a different city,
chunks.st: If the gentiles brought him to a different city
chunks.stMore: that was surrounded by walls,

chunks.en: or put him in a pen or a stable,
chunks.st: or if they put him into a pen or a stable,
chunks.stMore: i.e., animal enclosures, the Sages disagree.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: ben Azaryah say,
chunks.st: ben Azarya say:

chunks.en: he may walk all of it.
chunks.st: He may walk about the entire city,
chunks.stMore: as the whole city is considered like four cubits.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva say:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he has only four amos.
chunks.st: He has only four cubits
chunks.stMore: from where he was placed.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבָּאוּ מִפְּרַנְדִּיסִין וְהִפְלִיגָה סְפִינָתָם בַּיָּם.
chunks.en: Once they came from Pelandarsin, and their ship sailed out into the sea.
chunks.st: The mishna relates: There was an incident where all of these Sages were coming from Pelandarsin, an overseas location, and their boat set sail on the sea
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat, taking them beyond their Shabbat limit.

words.note: A faraway place across the sea.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya walked

chunks.en: Azaryah walked all over the ship.
chunks.st: about the entire boat,
chunks.stMore: as they hold that the entire boat is considered like four cubits, while

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva

chunks.en: did not move past four amos,
chunks.st: did not move beyond four cubits,

chunks.en: because they wanted to be strict with themselves.
chunks.st: as they sought to be stringent with themselves.

summary: Once the ship came into port only after dark. Rabban Gamliel told the others they could get off, because he had seen that they were inside the Shabbos area before nightfall.

chunks.en: One time they did not come
chunks.st: The mishna further relates that on one occasion, they did not enter

chunks.en: into the port until it was dark.
chunks.st: the port [namel] until after nightfall
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat eve.

chunks.en: They said to Rabban Gamliel,
chunks.st: The others said to Rabban Gamliel:

chunks.en: May we get off?
chunks.st: What is the halakha with regard to alighting
chunks.stMore: from the boat at this time? In other words, were we already within the city’s limit before Shabbat commenced?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: You are allowed,
chunks.st: You are permitted
chunks.stMore: to alight,

chunks.en: because I was already watching,
chunks.st: as I was watching, and

chunks.he: וְהָיִינוּ בְתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם עַד שֶׁלֹּא חֲשֵׁכָה:
chunks.en: and we were inside the Shabbos area before it got dark.
chunks.st: I observed that we were already within the city’s limit before nightfall. We acquired our resting place in the city during the twilight period. Therefore, it is permitted to walk throughout the city even after nightfall.

summary: Someone who was allowed to leave his Shabbos area to help, and then finds out he is not needed, gets 2000 amos from where he is. People who go out to save lives may go back home.

chunks.en: Someone who went out with permission, and they told him,
chunks.st: With regard to one who was permitted to leave his Shabbat limit, i.e., he went out to testify that he had seen the new moon or for some life-saving purpose, and they said to him
chunks.stMore: along the way:

chunks.en: It was already done,
chunks.st: The action has already been performed,
chunks.stMore: and there is no need for you to travel for that purpose,

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ.
chunks.en: has two thousand amos in every direction.
chunks.st: he has two thousand cubits in each direction
chunks.stMore: from the location where he was standing when this was told to him.

chunks.en: If he was inside his Shabbos area,
chunks.st: If he was within his original limit,

chunks.en: it is as if he never left.
chunks.st: it is considered as if he had not left
chunks.stMore: his limit, and he may return to his original location.

chunks.en: For all who go out to save lives
chunks.st: The Sages formulated a principle: All who go out to battle and save lives

chunks.en: may go back to their places.
chunks.st: may return to their original locations on Shabbat.

summary: A person sat down on the road, and after Shabbos began he saw he was close to a town. Rabbi Meir says he may not go in because he did not plan to; Rabbi Yehudah says he may, and tells a story about Rabbi Tarfon.

chunks.en: Someone who sat down on the road,
chunks.st: With regard to a person who was sitting along the road
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat eve toward nightfall, unaware that he was within the city’s Shabbat limit,

chunks.he: וְעָמַד, וְרָאָה וַהֲרֵי הוּא סָמוּךְ לָעִיר,
chunks.en: and got up, and saw that he was close to a town,
chunks.st: and when he stood up after Shabbat had already commenced, he saw that he was near the town,
chunks.stMore: i.e., within its limit,

chunks.en: since he did not mean to be there,
chunks.st: since he had not intended
chunks.stMore: to acquire his place of residence in the town,

chunks.en: may not go in,
chunks.st: he may not enter
chunks.stMore: it, but rather he measures two thousand cubits from his place;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he may go in. Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: He may enter the town. Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: there was a story,
chunks.st: It once happened that

chunks.en: and Rabbi Tarfon went in without planning to.
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon entered a town on Shabbat without intention from the beginning of Shabbat to establish residence in the city.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

summary: Someone fell asleep on the road and did not know that Shabbos had started. The Rabbis argue whether he gets 2000 amos or only four amos, and in which direction.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיָּשֵׁן בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְלֹא יָדַע שֶׁחֲשֵׁכָה,
chunks.en: Someone who slept on the road and did not know it got dark,
chunks.st: With regard to one who was sleeping along the road on Shabbat eve and did not know that night had fallen,

chunks.he: יֵשׁ לוֹ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ,
chunks.en: has two thousand amos in every direction,
chunks.st: he has two thousand cubits in each direction;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri,
chunks.stMore: who maintains that knowledge and awareness are not necessary for one to acquire residence, but rather, a person’s presence in a given location establishes residence there.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he has only four amos.
chunks.st: He has only four cubits,
chunks.stMore: as since he did not knowingly acquire residence, he did not establish a Shabbat limit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: and he is in the middle of them.
chunks.st: He has only four cubits total and he is in the middle of them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he has two cubits in each direction.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he may walk in whatever direction he wants.
chunks.st: He may walk four cubits in any direction he wishes.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאִם בֵּרֵר לוֹ,
chunks.en: And Rabbi Yehudah agrees that once he chose a direction,
chunks.st: But Rabbi Yehuda agrees that if he selected for himself

chunks.en: he cannot change his mind.
chunks.st: the direction in which he wants to walk those four cubits, he cannot retract and walk four cubits in a different direction.

summary: When two or three people who each have only four amos stand near each other, they may share food only where their spaces overlap. Rabbi Shimon compares this to three courtyards.

chunks.en: If there were two people,
chunks.st: With regard to a case where there were two

chunks.en: and part of the four amos of one
chunks.st: people in this situation, positioned in such a way that part of the four cubits of one

chunks.en: is inside the four amos of the other,
chunks.st: were subsumed within the four cubits of the other,

chunks.en: they may bring food and eat in the middle,
chunks.st: they may each bring food and eat together in the shared area in the middle,

chunks.en: as long as one does not take things out from
chunks.st: provided that the one does not carry anything from his

chunks.en: his own space into his friend's space.
chunks.st: four-cubit limit into that of his fellow.

chunks.en: If there were three,
chunks.st: With regard to a case where there were three

chunks.en: and the middle one's space overlaps both of theirs,
chunks.st: people in this situation, and certain parts of the four cubits of the middle one were subsumed within the respective limits of each of the others,
chunks.stMore: so that he shared a certain area with each of them,

chunks.he: הוּא מֻתָּר עִמָּהֶן וְהֵן מֻתָּרִין עִמּוֹ,
chunks.en: he is allowed with them and they are allowed with him,
chunks.st: he is permitted to eat with either of them, and they are both permitted to eat with him;

chunks.he: וּשְׁנַיִם הַחִיצוֹנִים אֲסוּרִים זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.
chunks.st: but the two outer ones are forbidden to eat with each other,
chunks.stMore: since they share no common area.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: What is this like?
chunks.st: To what is this comparable?

chunks.en: Like three courtyards that open one
chunks.st: It is like three courtyards that open into one another,

chunks.en: into the next, and open into the public street.
chunks.st: and also open into a public domain.

chunks.en: If both made an eiruv with the middle one,
chunks.st: If the two outer courtyards established an eiruv with the middle one,

chunks.he: הִיא מֻתֶּרֶת עִמָּהֶם וְהֵן מֻתָּרוֹת עִמָּהּ,
chunks.en: it is allowed with them and they are allowed with it,
chunks.st: the middle one is permitted to carry to the two outer ones, and they are permitted to carry to it,

chunks.he: וּשְׁתַּיִם הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ:
chunks.en: but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.
chunks.st: but the two outer courtyards are prohibited to carry from one to the other, as they did not establish an eiruv with one another.

summary: A traveler who sees a tree before Shabbos can make it his Shabbos home by naming its trunk exactly. Then he may walk 2000 amos to the tree and 2000 more from there.

chunks.en: Someone who was traveling on the road and it got dark,
chunks.st: With regard to one who was coming along the way on Shabbat eve, and it grew dark while he was traveling,

chunks.en: and he knew of a tree or a fence,
chunks.st: and he was familiar with a tree or a fence
chunks.stMore: located two thousand cubits from his current location, and two thousand cubits from his house,

chunks.en: and he said, My Shabbos place is under it,
chunks.st: and he said: My residence is beneath that tree,
chunks.stMore: rather than in his present location,

chunks.en: he did not say anything.
chunks.explain: "Under it" is too big a place to count.
chunks.st: he has not said anything,
chunks.stMore: as he did not establish a fixed location as his residence.

chunks.en: But if he said: My Shabbos place is at its trunk,
chunks.st: If, however, he said: My residence is at the tree’s trunk,

chunks.en: he may walk from where his feet are up to
chunks.st: he acquired residence there, and he may therefore walk from the place he is standing to the trunk

chunks.en: its trunk, two thousand amos,
chunks.st: of the tree two thousand cubits

chunks.en: and from its trunk to his house, two thousand amos.
chunks.st: away, and from the trunk of the tree to his house, an additional two thousand cubits.

chunks.he: נִמְצָא מְהַלֵּךְ מִשֶּׁחֲשֵׁכָה אַרְבַּעַת אֲלָפִים אַמָּה:
chunks.en: So after dark he may walk four thousand amos.
chunks.st: Consequently, he walks after nightfall a total of four thousand cubits.

summary: If he does not know a place to pick, he may say "My Shabbos place is right here," and he gets 2000 amos all around. The Rabbis argue whether that space is measured as a circle or a square.

chunks.en: If he does not know of a tree,
chunks.st: If one is not familiar
chunks.stMore: with a tree or any other noticeable landmark,

chunks.en: or he does not know the halachah well,
chunks.st: or if he is not an expert in the halakha,
chunks.stMore: unaware that residence can be established from a distance,

chunks.en: and he said, My Shabbos place is right here,
chunks.st: and he said: My residence is at my current location,

chunks.en: his place gets him two thousand
chunks.st: then his presence at his current location acquires for him

chunks.en: amos in every direction.
chunks.st: the right to walk two thousand cubits in each direction.
chunks.stMore: The manner in which the two thousand cubits are measured is the subject of a tannaitic dispute.

chunks.he: עֲגֻלּוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס.
chunks.en: In a circle, says Rabbi Chanina ben Antignos.
chunks.st: These cubits are measured circularly, i.e., as a circle with a radius of two thousand cubits; this is the statement of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigenos.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: square, like a square board,
chunks.st: These are measured squarely, i.e., as a square tablet,
chunks.stMore: with each side measuring four thousand cubits,

chunks.en: so that he gains the corners.
chunks.st: so that he gains the corners. He is permitted to walk from the middle to the corners of the square as well, a distance of approximately 2,800 cubits.

summary: A poor person can make an eiruv by walking to a place and saying "This is my Shabbos home." Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue whether a rich person may also do this.

chunks.en: And this is what they said,
chunks.st: And this is the meaning of that which the Sages said:

chunks.en: A poor man makes an eiruv with his feet.
chunks.explain: He walks there instead of putting down food.
chunks.st: The pauper establishes an eiruv with his feet,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one who does not have the bread required to establish an eiruv may walk anywhere within his Shabbat limit and declare: This is my residence, and his Shabbat limit is measured from that location.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: we only have this for a poor man.
chunks.st: We have this leniency in effect only for a pauper,
chunks.stMore: who does not have food for two meals. However, one who has bread may only establish residence with bread.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: both a poor man and a rich man.
chunks.st: This leniency is in effect for both a pauper and a wealthy person.

chunks.en: They only said to make an eiruv with bread
chunks.st: The Sages said that one establishes an eiruv with bread only

chunks.en: to make it easier for the rich man,
chunks.st: in order to be lenient with the wealthy person,

chunks.en: so he does not have to go out and make an eiruv with his feet.
chunks.st: so that he need not exert himself and go out and establish an eiruv with his feet. Instead, he can appoint an agent to place bread for him in that location. This, however, does not negate the option of personally going to that location in order to establish residence without bread.

summary: If someone set out before Shabbos to make his Shabbos home in another town and his friend sent him back, Rabbi Yehudah says only he may go there on Shabbos. Rabbi Meir says he is like a donkey driver and camel driver.

chunks.en: Someone who set out to go to a town
chunks.st: If a person set out to go on a Shabbat eve to a town

chunks.en: where people make an eiruv, and his friend sent him back,
chunks.st: for which an eiruv is established in order to go there on Shabbat, and another person caused him to return home,

chunks.en: he is allowed to go, and all
chunks.st: he himself is permitted to go

chunks.en: the people of the town are forbidden,
chunks.st: to that city on Shabbat, and for all the other residents of the town it is prohibited
chunks.stMore: to go there.

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לְעָרֵב וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: anyone who could make an eiruv and did not,
chunks.st: Anyone who can establish an eiruv, and negated his residence in his original place, and did not establish an eiruv,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he did not at least state that he seeks to establish residence somewhere else,

chunks.en: he is like a donkey driver and a camel driver.
chunks.st: is likened to both a donkey driver, who walks behind the animal and prods it, and a camel driver, who walks before the animal and leads it, in the sense that he is pulled in two opposite directions. Due to the uncertainty with regard to the location of his Shabbat limit, his movement is restricted as though his residence was established in both his city and at a location along the way to the other city. He may not venture beyond two thousand cubits from either location.

summary: Someone who went out past his Shabbos limit, or was outside it when Shabbos started, may not come back in. Some Rabbis say a little bit outside is still all right.

chunks.en: Someone who went out past the Shabbos limit,
chunks.st: One who intentionally, not for the purpose of performing a mitzva, went out beyond his Shabbat limit,

chunks.en: even one amah,
chunks.st: even if only one cubit,

chunks.en: may not come back in.
chunks.st: may not reenter.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: two amos, he may come in,
chunks.st: If he went out two cubits he may reenter;

chunks.en: three, he may not come in.
chunks.st: however, if he went out three cubits he may not reenter.

chunks.en: Someone who was outside the Shabbos limit when it got dark,
chunks.st: With regard to one for whom it grew dark while he was traveling outside the Shabbat limit of the town where he was heading,

chunks.en: even one amah,
chunks.st: even if he was only one cubit

chunks.en: may not go in.
chunks.st: outside the limit he may not enter the town.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even fifteen amos,
chunks.st: Even if he was fifteen cubits

chunks.he: יִכָּנֵס, שֶׁאֵין הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת מְמַצִּין אֶת הַמִּדּוֹת,
chunks.en: he may go in, because the measurers do not mark the full amount,
chunks.st: beyond the limit he may enter the town, because the surveyors do not precisely demarcate the measures;
chunks.stMore: rather, they mark the Shabbat limit within the two thousand cubits,

chunks.en: because of people who make mistakes.
chunks.st: due to those who err.
